Cartesian coordinates zoomed to a genomic locus

Source: R/coord-locus.R
coord_locus.Rd

Sets the x-axis of a plot to a genomic window. Every layer whose data has a seqnames column is subset to rows on the window's chromosome that overlap the window, before aesthetics are evaluated, so discrete scales only show levels present in the window. Layers without a seqnames column are left untouched.

Also adds an x-axis scale named after the chromosome (e.g. "Chr 3 (Mbp)") with labels in Mbp for windows wider than 10 kbp and bp otherwise. Add your own scale_x_continuous() after coord_locus() to override it.

coord_locus() is coord_loci() with a single window, and x positions are the genomic coordinates themselves.

Usage

coord_locus(window_of_interest, flank = 0, expand = TRUE, clip = "on")

Arguments

window_of_interest

Genomic window as a string, e.g. "chr3:187734001-187751500".

flank

Number of bp to extend both ends of the window, default: 0

expand

If TRUE, the default, adds a small expansion to the window limits.

clip

Should drawing be clipped to the extent of the plot panel? Default: "on"

Value

List of a coord and an x-axis scale, added to a plot with +
